run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-15T11:47:16Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/fraud-detection is explained by a small, recurring set of error spans that fraud-detection emits on its long-lived flagd client call. In the window 10:47:16–12:00:16Z, fraud-detection produced 469 spans in traces_span_metrics_calls_total and 12 of them are STATUS_CODE_ERROR, all on two flagd operations: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (10) and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt (2). In Jaeger those EventStream client spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) with durations of ~594–602 s, i.e. the client's ~10-minute stream deadline; the matching flagd (v0.12.8) server spans run ~522–556 s, end mostly with rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and in some cases carry the exact description "stream closed due to server-side timeout". The same signature appears for the ad service, so the stream closure originates at flagd rather than in fraud-detection's code. Because the alert condition is an error rate above 0, these recurring stream-renewal errors are enough to keep the ratio positive: observed 12/469 ≈ 2.6% for fraud-detection, comparable in magnitude to the alert payload's 0.0222. flagd is up (1/1 ready, pod 0 restarts) and fraud-detection is up (10/10 ready, all pods 0 restarts), and fraud-detection's Kafka consumer spans carry no error status, so no evidence supports a flagd outage or a Kafka-caused request failure; a concurrent shipping 'EOF' checkout failure at 11:07:11 is a separate chain that contains no fraud-detection span. Caveats that keep this partial: the RequestErrorRate rule itself could not be retrieved (rules query returned no data), and span-metric samples in this Prometheus end around 11:17Z, so the alert's state at 11:47:16Z could not be reproduced.

claims.text: In the 73-minute window ending 2026-11-15T12:00:16Z, service fraud-detection had 469 spans in traces_span_metrics_calls_total and 12 spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

All 12 error spans of fraud-detection are on flagd client operations: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (10 error spans) and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt (2 error spans). Its Kafka consumer operations 'orders process' (230 spans) and 'orders receive' (221 spans) were only returned with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no error-status series for those operations was returned for this window.

fraud-detection's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream client spans in Jaeger have error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) with durations 594101234–601796702 µs (about 600 s); the 10 such spans shown start between 2026-11-15T10:55:53Z and 2026-11-15T10:59:41Z and end around 11:05:55–11:07:39Z.

The matching flagd server spans (service flagd, service_version v0.12.8) for the same EventStream calls run 522403796–556200065 µs; 2 of the 9 shown carry otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 while the other 7 end with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

Trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 contains exactly two spans: fraud-detection's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream client span of 599999905 µs with rpc.grpc.status_code=4, and a child flagd server span of 553397947 µs with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

The same flagd EventStream signature exists for a different service: ad has flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream client spans with error=true and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, 596886931–604202243 µs, and corresponding flagd v0.12.8 server spans of 522403796–538800214 µs (4 with rpc.grpc.status_code=0, 1 with status description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" and code 4).

flagd and fraud-detection are up: deployment flagd 1/1 ready and fraud-detection 10/10 ready; all 10 fraud-detection pods (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-*) are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and start times 10:51:18–10:54:21Z; flagd pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx is Running with 0 restarts and start time 10:53:10Z.
Two Kafka pods show container restarts with the last termination reason Error and exit code 1: kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w (restartCount 3) and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr (restartCount 1).

Error-status spans are not unique to fraud-detection in this window: max cumulative error counters per service are frontend 1829, frontend-proxy 848, payment 40, ad 31, checkout 27, shipping 24, fraud-detection 12, recommendation 7, accounting 5. At 11:10:00Z frontend alone showed 1829 error spans and 26048 UNSET spans.

A separate checkout failure occurred at 11:07:11Z: checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span ended with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and otel.status_description "shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post \"http://shipping:8080/get-quote\": EOF", propagating HTTP 500 to frontend and frontend-proxy; the trace contains no fraud-detection span.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo between 11:06:35Z and 11:09:39Z contain nothing about flagd or fraud-detection; they are HPA FailedGetResourceMetric / FailedComputeMetricsReplicas warnings and recommendation scale-down events from 10 to 8 replicas at 11:07:10Z and 8 to 7 at 11:08:10Z with reason "All metrics below target".

Primary explanation: the alert fires because fraud-detection keeps producing STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on its long-lived flagd EventStream/ResolveInt client calls (gRPC code 4, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED at the ~600 s stream deadline), and the spanmetrics connector counts them as error spans. With a threshold of "error rate above 0" the recurring stream-renewal errors keep the ratio positive; the observed 12 error spans of 469 total spans (≈2.6%) is of the same order as the 0.0222 reported in the alert payload.

Deepest supported cause: the flagd side closes the long-lived evaluation EventStream at about 9.2 minutes (server spans 522–556 s, description "stream closed due to server-side timeout", several ending with code 0), while clients keep the call open until their ~600 s deadline and record DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; the identical pattern in ad indicates flagd/flagd-client stream handling rather than a fraud-detection-specific defect.

flagd being down or unavailable as the cause of fraud-detection's errors is rejected: flagd is 1/1 ready with a 0-restart pod, and most flagd server EventStream spans end with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 while the client span still records code 4 when its own ~600 s deadline expires.

The Kafka pod restarts (kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w restartCount 3, kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr restartCount 1, last termination reason Error exit 1) are not supported as the cause of fraud-detection's request error rate: fraud-detection's own Kafka consumer spans 'orders process' and 'orders receive' were returned only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no error series.

The 11:07:11Z shipping 'EOF' checkout failure is rejected as the cause of the fraud-detection alert: that trace's error spans are checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator spans failing on the shipping dependency, and it contains no fraud-detection span.

The recommendation scale-down from 10 to 8 replicas at 11:07:10Z and 8 to 7 at 11:08:10Z, which is roughly coincident with the flagd stream closures, is rejected as this cause: the events attribute it to the HPA (reason "All metrics below target") and there is no fraud-detection evidence linking it to the flagd client error spans.

Confirm the RequestErrorRate PromQL in the Prometheus/Alertmanager config that produced this alert (the registered Prometheus returned no rule set), and if it counts all spans, exclude the long-lived streaming client span flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (or restrict to server-side operations) and/or require a sustained error rate rather than "above 0", so that 10-minute stream renewals do not page.

Review the flagd v0.12.8 / OpenFeature-provider EventStream deadline and keepalive configuration (server closes at ~9.2 min, client records DEADLINE_EXCEEDED at ~10 min) and align the two values so stream renewal does not appear as a failed call.

Check why span-metric samples stop around 11:17Z (otel-collector otel-collector-564d9c7987-bln8k and the Prometheus scrape of instance 100.96.3.168:8889) so that alert evaluation after that point is based on fresh data.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for the whole rule set, so its exact PromQL, threshold and for-duration are unknown and the reported value 0.02222222222222222 could not be reproduced exactly.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total samples stop around 11:17Z for all services; instant queries at the alert start 2026-11-15T11:47:16Z for fraud-detection and frontend returned no data, so the metric state at alert time (and whether the flagd stream errors continued after ~11:17) is unknown.

Pod logs are unavailable in this environment: fetch_pod_logs for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l and flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx returned 0 lines for 10:47–12:00Z, so application-side flag evaluation failures/fallbacks cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Jaeger returned no trace for the flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt error spans that spanmetrics records (2 error spans), and no fraud-detection traces after 11:07:39Z, so the ResolveInt failures are unexamined.

flagd's own metrics are not present in this Prometheus (queries for flagd.* metric names and for service_name="flagd" returned no data), so flagd-internal behaviour behind the ~9.2-minute stream timeout (memory, goroutines, stream deadline settings) could not be verified; the flagd container has GOMEMLIMIT=60MiB and no restart or OOMKilled record.

The cause of the Kafka container restarts with exit code 1 (kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w, kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr) is unknown and its own logs were not read; it is not tied to the fraud-detection error spans by any evidence observed.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether a config/image rollout (all otel-demo pods were created 10:51–11:02Z) relates to the flagd stream timeouts cannot be established.

No data was obtained on whether the customers/order flow was actually affected: fraud-detection's consumer spans show no error status, but the application logs needed to confirm successful flag-evaluation fallbacks are unavailable.
next_steps: Read the Prometheus/Alertmanager rule definition for RequestErrorRate (and its namespace/service filters) to confirm which series and threshold drive the 0.0222 value.

Inspect otel-collector (otel-collector-564d9c7987-bln8k) and Prometheus scrape health around 11:15–11:47Z to explain why span-metric samples stop around 11:17Z, and confirm whether this is a telemetry-pipeline outage.

Review the flagd EventStream deadline/timeout configuration for flagd v0.12.8 and the OpenFeature providers used by fraud-detection and ad, and decide whether the periodic DEADLINE_EXCEEDED should be treated as expected stream renewal.

Review pod logs and Kafka broker logs for the restarted Kafka pods (kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w, kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr) to establish their own failure reason, without attributing it to the fraud-detection alert.
Investigate the separate shipping dependency failure seen at 11:07:11Z (POST http://shipping:8080/get-quote -> EOF) under its own alert if one exists.
